anchors.phrase: Now let's look at the complexity.
anchors.purpose: Complexity analysis transition; title card fades in.

anchors.phrase: The pivot scan moves from right to left.
anchors.purpose: Pass 1 visualization: right-to-left pivot scan.

anchors.phrase: In the worst case, it can inspect the whole array.
anchors.purpose: Pass 1 cost: at most N operations (<= N).

anchors.phrase: The successor scan also moves from right to left, over at most the array length.
anchors.purpose: Pass 2 cost: at most N operations (<= N).

anchors.phrase: And the final reverse touches at most the suffix once.
anchors.purpose: Pass 3 cost: at most N/2 swaps (<= N).

anchors.phrase: These are separate linear passes.
anchors.purpose: Passes are sequential, not nested.

anchors.phrase: We do not multiply them.
anchors.purpose: Additive math: N + N + N = 3N.

anchors.phrase: So the total time complexity is O of n,
anchors.purpose: Time complexity stamp: O(N) linear time.

anchors.phrase: and we only use a few index variables.
anchors.purpose: Memory: only i, j, left, right, n used.

anchors.phrase: So the extra space is O of 1.
anchors.purpose: Space complexity stamp: O(1) in-place auxiliary space.

anchors.phrase: Now compare that with brute force.
anchors.purpose: Contrast section: Brute Force vs Optimal Method.

anchors.phrase: With n distinct values, there can be n factorial permutations.
anchors.purpose: Combinatorial explosion: N! permutations growth.

anchors.phrase: Generating and storing all of them is already factorial scale work.
anchors.purpose: Exponential/factorial wall of generation and storage.

anchors.phrase: And sorting them adds even more work.
anchors.purpose: Lexicographic sorting penalty adds further factorial work.

anchors.phrase: The optimal method works directly on the current array.
anchors.purpose: Contrast conclusion: in-place surgical transformation vs massive generation.

anchors.phrase: There are a few mistakes to avoid.
anchors.purpose: Common mistakes transition card.

anchors.phrase: For the pivot, we need a strict increase. We are looking for nums at i smaller than nums at i plus 1.
anchors.purpose: Mistake 1: Must be strict inequality nums[i] < nums[i+1].

anchors.phrase: Equal values do not qualify.
anchors.purpose: Negative example: 4 < 4 is FALSE. Never treat equal as dip.

anchors.phrase: For the successor, we also need a value strictly greater than the pivot.
anchors.purpose: Mistake 2: Successor condition must be strictly greater (nums[j] > nums[i]).

anchors.phrase: Equal is not enough.
anchors.purpose: Successor equality rejection: nums[j] == nums[i] leaves prefix identical.

anchors.phrase: Another mistake is choosing any greater value from the suffix.
anchors.purpose: Mistake 3: Picking an arbitrary larger value breaks the immediate successor.

anchors.phrase: We need the smallest possible increase.
anchors.purpose: Requirement: Smallest strictly greater value.

anchors.phrase: That is why we scan from the right.
anchors.purpose: Right-to-left scan guarantees the first greater element is the smallest.

anchors.phrase: And after the swap, reverse from i plus 1.
anchors.purpose: Mistake 4: Correct reversal range starts at i+1.

anchors.phrase: Do not reverse from i.
anchors.purpose: Off-by-one warning: reversing from i destroys the newly placed pivot.

anchors.phrase: Now consider a fully decreasing array, 3, 2, 1.
anchors.purpose: Edge Case 1: Fully decreasing array [3, 2, 1].

anchors.phrase: There is no pivot.
anchors.purpose: Condition check: no dip found, i terminates at -1.

anchors.phrase: So this is already the largest permutation.
anchors.purpose: Semantic meaning: lexicographically maximal.

anchors.phrase: Reverse the whole array,
anchors.purpose: Action: left = -1 + 1 = 0, reverses whole array.

anchors.phrase: and we get 1, 2, 3.
anchors.purpose: Result: [1, 2, 3] smallest permutation (wraparound).

anchors.phrase: If the array is already increasing, like 1, 2, 3.
anchors.purpose: Edge Case 2: Already increasing array [1, 2, 3].

anchors.phrase: The pivot is near the right side, so only a small suffix changes.
anchors.purpose: Pivot at index n-2 immediately; swaps with last element, suffix length 0.

anchors.phrase: For a single value, there is nothing to change.
anchors.purpose: Edge Case 3: Single element array [x] (n=1, i=-1, reverse loop terminates).

anchors.phrase: And duplicate values are also handled naturally, because both important comparisons are strict.
anchors.purpose: Edge Case 4: Duplicates handled seamlessly by strict < and strict >.

anchors.phrase: No special duplicate case is needed.
anchors.purpose: Final synthesis: Robustness of optimal algorithm verified across all cases.
